grand_strategy.reading: South Africa under Ramaphosa's government of national unity has moved from a balance between the West and the Global South to a deliberate Global South stance, with the ICJ case, BRICS and the 2025 G20 presidency as its instruments of standing. The United States is its main rival in 2025-26, but the rivalry runs on tariffs, aid and the Afrikaner refugee question rather than on existence, and the AGOA lapse shows how cheaply Washington can apply pressure. China is the commercial anchor, and the trade deal in preparation is the test of whether Pretoria can turn minerals into value. The constraints are at home (the grid, the rand, a stalled economy) and in the neighbourhood (Nigeria's leadership claim, a withdrawn DRC force), so the stance is louder than the capacity behind it.

stances.note: Rival, not adversary: aid, trade and the refugee question are contested, and neither side seeks the other's end. Mirror of the USA card, same sources: Executive Order 14204 cut aid (7 Feb 2025), the Ramaphosa-Trump White House meeting of 21 May 2025 turned on claims of white-farmer killings, the 30% tariff applied from 7 August 2025, AGOA lapsed on 30 September 2025 and was renewed only to the end of 2026, and South Africa was left out of the 2026 G20 in Miami (Truth Social, 26 Nov 2025). Trend cooling. Bond grievance, South Africa's side (our reading): the aid cut and the Afrikaner refugee order are read in Pretoria as an attack on the state. The expulsion of the US ambassador is in the USA card but no source for it is cited here, so it is not counted.
